edition_note: Friday premarket, 06:00 ET snapshot. Futures vs prior contract close. Cash indices and BTC: completed Nov 19 bars. Official Treasury yields: Nov 18; not live. Premarket ETF moves are separate from their regular-session returns.
client_frame_short:
How can Anthropic have a good first day and tech stocks still fall? Investors were willing to fund one company, but **buying its shares is not the same as buying the whole AI industry**. Amazon and Google benefit from a more valuable stake; that does not tell us what they will earn on their next data center.

Chip shares are down again before the open, while the Dow futures are slightly higher. There’s no need to trade a diversified account on that split. I’m watching whether the selling spreads beyond tech after the open and how consumers describe inflation later this morning.
client_frame:
Thursday gave us two different answers. Anthropic ended its debut at $97.17 versus an $83 offer, but the Nasdaq-100 finished lower. Early Friday, the semiconductor ETF fell more than the Nasdaq tracker. Investors can like the price of one offering and still demand better evidence that its suppliers will earn an adequate return. (Quote API; Anthropic)

Amazon and Alphabet have direct stakes in Anthropic. A higher share price raises the implied value of those existing holdings, not cash received. A better-funded customer also matters to its cloud providers. Neither channel guarantees that the additional servers, power and buildings will produce attractive margins. (SEC offering materials)

The December rate distribution is a separate piece of the picture. CME’s November 19 probabilities put more weight on a quarter-point increase than its previous reading, but less on a half-point increase. That is a shift toward the smaller of two increases, not a fresh move toward a larger hike. (CME; Federal Reserve)

For clients: a concentrated account and a diversified account need different conversations. The useful check today is whether the losses stay concentrated in chips or spread to the rest of the market. Near-term spending needs are a better reason to revisit risk than the first two trading sessions of one stock.
geo_headlines: **Overnight futures:** Nasdaq-100 futures fell 1.07%, S&P futures slipped 0.34% and Dow futures edged up 0.24%. The weakness is not uniform.
**Asian session:** Equities fell in Japan and South Korea after the US selloff. The sequence is clear; it is not proof that the IPO caused those declines. (Reuters)
**Oil and gold:** WTI futures slipped 0.80% and gold futures fell 2.56% from their respective prior closes.
